LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The global (top-level) scope of this PKGBUILD consists entirely of variable and array assignments (``pkgname``, ``source``, ``sha512sums``, etc.) and two function definitions (``build()`` and ``package()``). Bash does not execute the body of a function defined with ``name() { ... }`` until the function is explicitly called, and ``makepkg --printsrcinfo`` only sources the file without calling ``build()`` or ``package()``.  

There are no command substitutions (``$(...)`` or backticks), no ``eval``, no ``exec``, and no invocations of ``curl``, ``wget``, ``base64``, or any other dangerous utilities anywhere in the global scope. The literal HTML entities (``&quot;``, ``&apos;``) present in the file prevent proper shell quoting, but they are inert characters that do not trigger command execution—they simply cause the affected variables to contain broken strings rather than valid values. No code outside the function bodies can execute during ``--printsrcinfo``.  Therefore, sourcing this file for metadata parsing is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>No dangerous global scope code.</summary>
</security_assessment>
